inlines.text: 建立在多年运营 Auto Router 的经验之上

blocks.text: Auto Router 即将迎来三岁生日。如果你几年前在某个智能体里设置了 openrouter/auto，今天它依然会为你选出最新的成本最优方案。我们积累了不少关于自动模型选择会在哪些地方出问题的经验，新一代产品正是为了避开这些问题而打造的。举几个例子：

blocks.text: 我们把 Auto Code 单独拆出来，专门针对编程框架做优化。以往版本的 Auto Router 最常被吐槽的，就是它在编程框架里的表现。Auto Code 更倾向于选择略贵一档、但能力与编程工作更匹配的模型。它更看重速度，因为你在写代码时响应快慢很关键。它对失败的惩罚也更重，所以在成败界限分明的工作上能更快纠偏。

blocks.text: 它在切换模型上很克制，以保住缓存收益。切换模型是有额外成本的，因为新模型要重建输入 token 缓存。只要调整推理强度就够用，Auto Router 就优先这么做；只有当收益值得放弃缓存时才会切换。在内测期间，它几乎每十个智能体回合就有九个停留在同一个模型上。

blocks.text: 模型路由建立在领先的提供商路由基础之上

inlines.text: 模型路由建立在领先的提供商路由基础之上

blocks.text: 模型路由器（如 Auto Router 和 Auto Code）决定由哪个模型来处理请求。提供商路由则决定由谁来提供这个模型。OpenRouter 从一开始就对每个请求做这件事：模型选定后，提供商路由器会根据你的提供商偏好、实时在线率与延迟、价格，以及某个提供商是否已持有你的提示词缓存，在托管该模型的提供商之间做出选择。

blocks.text: 请求如何经过 Auto Router

inlines.text: 请求如何经过 Auto Router
Auto Router 先收窄模型池。护栏、零数据留存、模型能力、提供商限制、BYOK 密钥，以及任何允许或排除的模型列表，共同决定哪些模型会被纳入考虑。
一个快速的决策模型来处理请求。它在一次调用中评估十一项内容，比如这是什么类型的任务、任务是否刚刚发生变化、难度有多大、速度是否重要、是否需要视觉能力或对代码库的了解，以及换用更大的模型、更多思考还是更便宜的模型会更合适。
路由策略负责选模型。它会权衡实时价格、缓存状态和基准测试表现，据此同时决定用哪个模型以及投入多少推理力度。
请求会走一遍直接请求该模型时相同的供应商路由，因此最终会落到该模型最合适的供应商上。
每一轮的结果都会影响下一轮的模型选择。路由器会把模型是否吃力、哪些内容已经缓存等信号带入下一次决策。

blocks.text: Today we’re launching the next generation of Auto Router. Taking all we’ve learned from running Auto Router for the past 3 years, we rebuilt it from the ground up on an entirely new technical foundation that outperforms the old router by up to 4× depending on the benchmark, with a routing step that is 3× faster at the p90 in our live test (0.65s against 1.96s).

blocks.text: What’s new in this generation

inlines.text: What’s new in this generation

blocks.text: The previous Auto Router relied on a couple of imprecise signals, such as task type, to drive model selection, a limit required to keep latency low and judgments consistent. The new Auto Router and Auto Code choose models by weighing eleven factors about each request and combining them with live pricing, provider health, and cache status.

blocks.text: This new process lets Auto Router work with any set of models. You can apply any governance policies, including guardrails, zero data retention requirements, provider restrictions, allowed model lists, and BYOK keys. Auto Router makes efficient choices from the models available to you.

blocks.text: In the previous generation, we also observed that the remarkable efficiency of the lowest cost models had caused Auto router to drift lower on cost per task, leaving out many exceptional models. We made a decision with this release to return to pricing closer to where Auto was a few months ago in order to introduce a greater variety of models. If you preferred the previous behavior, you can set the cost_tier to low to get similar cost performance.

blocks.text: Built upon years of lessons from running Auto Router

inlines.text: Built upon years of lessons from running Auto Router

blocks.text: Auto Router is coming up on its third birthday. If you set openrouter/auto in an agent years ago, you’re still getting the latest cost-optimal choice today. We’ve learned a lot about where automatic model selection goes wrong, and built the new generation to avoid those problems. Some examples:

inlines.text: Auto Router is coming up on its third birthday. If you set
openrouter/auto

in an agent years ago, you’re still getting the latest cost-optimal choice today. We’ve learned a lot about where automatic model selection goes wrong, and built the new generation to avoid those problems. Some examples:

blocks.text: We separated out Auto Code to optimize for harnesses. The most common complaint about previous versions of Auto Router was how it performed in coding harnesses. Auto Code favors a slightly more expensive tier of models whose strengths match coding work. It weighs speed more heavily because responsiveness matters while you build. It also penalizes failures more harshly, so it course corrects faster on work where success and failure are clear cut.

inlines.text: We separated out Auto Code to optimize for harnesses.

The most common complaint about previous versions of Auto Router was how it performed in coding harnesses. Auto Code favors a slightly more expensive tier of models whose strengths match coding work. It weighs speed more heavily because responsiveness matters while you build. It also penalizes failures more harshly, so it course corrects faster on work where success and failure are clear cut.

blocks.text: It’s restrained about switching to protect caching benefits. Switching models costs extra while the new model rebuilds the input token cache. Auto Router favors a change in reasoning effort when that’s enough, and switches only when the gain is worth the cache it gives up. In our beta period it stayed on the same model for nearly nine of every ten agent turns.

blocks.text: It adapts to failures. When a session is going wrong in ways that point at the model, such as the same error coming back or tests failing after an edit, those signals raise the odds of a switch. That makes it much less likely a session stays stuck with a model that was the wrong pick early on.

blocks.text: Model Routing built upon the leading Provider Routing foundation

inlines.text: Model Routing built upon the leading Provider Routing foundation

blocks.text: Model routers like Auto Router and Auto Code pick which model will process the request. Provider routing picks who will serve that model. OpenRouter has done this for every request since the beginning: once the model is picked, the provider router chooses among the providers hosting it using your provider preferences, live uptime and latency, price, and whether a provider already holds your prompt cache.

blocks.text: A model router can only be as good as the underlying provider router. We built Auto Router to be aware of our entire catalog, so it adapts to governance restrictions, benchmark results, and market signal from new model releases as they happen. Every one of the 600+ models on OpenRouter enters the consideration set the day it’s added, and benchmarks and popularity signals decide whether it earns a place in the cost-optimal set.

blocks.text: How a request moves through Auto Router

inlines.text: How a request moves through Auto Router
Auto Router narrows the model pool. Guardrails, zero data retention, model capabilities, provider restrictions, BYOK keys, and any allowed or excluded model lists decide which models are considered.

A fast decision model processes the request. In one call it rates eleven things, such as what kind of task this is, whether the task just changed, how hard it is, whether speed matters, whether it needs vision or knowledge of a codebase, and whether a bigger model, more thinking, or a cheaper model would serve it better.
The routing policy chooses the model. It weighs live prices, cache status, and benchmark performance to pick both the model and the reasoning effort.
The request goes through the same provider routing a direct request to that model would, so it lands on the best provider for that model.
The results of each turn inform the next turn’s model selection. The router carries signals like whether the model is struggling and what’s already cached into the next decision.

blocks.text: Routers versus single models

inlines.text: Routers versus single models

blocks.text: Benchmarks consistently show that no router on the market beats the single best frontier model at every point on the cost and quality curve. The new Auto Router is no exception, and we publish its benchmarks to show its strengths and weaknesses plainly.

inlines.text: Benchmarks consistently show that no router on the market beats the single best frontier model at every point on the cost and quality curve. The new Auto Router is no exception, and we publish its benchmarks to show its strengths and weaknesses plainly.

blocks.text: Routers earn their place when the work is varied, when an organization needs to hold costs steady, and for people who don’t have the time or interest to keep up with the constant stream of model releases. Choosing Auto Router or Auto Code over a single model trades a little peak performance for consistent, cost efficient performance over time.

blocks.text: What is the difference between Auto Router and Auto Code?

inlines.text: What is the difference between Auto Router and Auto Code?

blocks.text: Both run on the same routing engine. Auto Router is the general purpose router for mixed traffic and general agents, and favors a cost-efficient tier of models. Auto Code is specialized for coding agents and harnesses, starts in a higher cost tier, and weighs measured pass rate, speed, and cost per solved task across models and reasoning efforts.

inlines.text: Is model routing the same as provider routing?
